units.zh: 陳三李曹劉
units.en: Chen, the Three Lis, Cao, and Liu
units.literal: Chen, Three Li's, Cao, Liu

units.zh: ◎陳夷行李紳李讓夷曹確劉瞻
units.en: ◎ Chen Yixing, Li Shen, Li Rangyi, Cao Que, and Liu Zhan
units.literal: ◎ Chen Yixing, Li Shen, Li Rangyi, Cao Que, Liu Zhan

units.en: (Liu Zhu)
units.literal: (Zhu)

units.zh: 李蔚
units.en: Li Wei
units.literal: Li Wei

units.zh: 陳夷行，字周道，其先江左諸陳也，世客潁川。
units.en: Chen Yixing, courtesy name Zhoudao, came from the Chen families of the lower Yangtze; his line had long resided in Yingchuan.
units.literal: Chen Yixing, styled Zhoudao, was descended from the various Chen clans of the Jiangzuo region; for generations his family had sojourned in Yingchuan.

units.zh: 由進士第，擢累起居郎、史館修撰。
units.en: Having passed the jinshi examination, he rose through the posts of diary attendant and historiography compiler.
units.literal: Through the jinshi degree he was promoted in succession to Attendant of the Imperial Diary and Compiler in the Historiography Institute.

units.zh: 以勞遷司封員外郎，凡再歲，以吏部郎中為翰林學士。
units.en: Rewarded for his labors with appointment as vice director in the Bureau of Appointments, he served there for two years before the Ministry of Personnel made him a Hanlin academician.
units.literal: For meritorious service he was transferred to Vice Director in the Bureau of Appointments; after two years in all he became a Hanlin academician from his post as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 莊恪太子在東宮，夷行兼侍讀，五日一謁，為太子講說。
units.en: While Crown Prince Zhuangke resided in the Eastern Palace, Yixing doubled as lecturer-in-attendance, visiting every five days to instruct the heir.
units.literal: When the Heir Apparent Zhuangke was in the Eastern Palace, Yixing also served as Lecturer-in-Attendance, paying court every five days to lecture the crown prince.

units.zh: 數遷至工部侍郎。
units.en: He was promoted repeatedly until he became vice minister of works.
units.literal: After several promotions he reached Vice Minister of Works.

units.zh: 開成二年，進同中書門下平章事。
units.en: In 837 he was made a co-director of the Chancellery with the title of chief minister.
units.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng he was advanced to Co-Director of the Chancellery with the designation Tong Zhongshu Menxia Pingzhangshi.

units.zh: 而楊嗣復、李玨相次輔政，夷行介特，雅不與合，每議論天子前，往往語相侵短。
units.en: Yang Sifu and Li Jue, however, were serving as chief ministers in succession; Yixing was stiff and independent by nature and clashed with them, and their exchanges before the emperor often turned personal.
units.literal: But Yang Sifu and Li Jue in turn held chief ministerial power; Yixing was upright and aloof and by nature did not harmonize with them—whenever they debated before the Son of Heaven their words often cut at one another.

units.zh: 夷行不能堪，輒引疾求去，文宗遣使者尉勞起之。
units.en: Unable to bear the friction, Yixing repeatedly cited illness to resign, until Wenzong sent messengers to comfort him and recall him to duty.
units.literal: Yixing could not endure it and repeatedly pleaded illness to resign; Emperor Wenzong sent envoys to console him and urge his return to office.

units.zh: 會以王彥威為忠武節度使，史孝章領邠寧，議皆出嗣復。
units.en: When Wang Yanwei was named military commissioner of Zhongwu and Shi Xiaozhang was put in charge of Binning, the appointments had all been Sifu's doing.
units.literal: It happened that Wang Yanwei was appointed military commissioner of Zhongwu and Shi Xiaozhang took charge of Binning—the deliberations all came from Sifu.

units.zh: 及夷行對延英，帝問：「除二鎮當否？」
units.en: At the Yanying audience Yixing was asked, "Were these two frontier appointments appropriate?"
units.literal: When Yixing responded at the Yanying Hall, the emperor asked: "Were the appointments to the two circuits appropriate?"

units.zh: 對曰：「茍自聖擇，無不當者。」
units.en: He answered, "If Your Majesty chose them yourself, every appointment is fitting."
units.literal: He replied: "If they were chosen by Your Sacred Majesty, none could be inappropriate."

units.zh: 嗣復曰：「若用人盡出上意而當，固善。
units.en: Sifu said, "If every choice that matches the emperor's wish is automatically right, that is well enough.
units.literal: Sifu said: "If every appointment that accords with the sovereign's will is good, that is fine.

units.zh: 如小不稱，下安得嘿然？」
units.en: But if something is even slightly unsuitable, how can ministers below keep quiet?"
units.literal: But if there is some slight unfitness, how can those below remain silent?"

units.zh: 夷行曰：「比奸臣數幹權，願陛下無倒持大阿，以鐏授人。」
units.en: Yixing said, "Treacherous ministers have lately seized power again and again; I beg Your Majesty not to grip the great sword by the blade and offer the hilt to someone else."
units.literal: Yixing said: "Lately treacherous ministers have repeatedly meddled in power; I beg Your Majesty not to hold the great sword reversed and hand the pommel to others."

units.zh: 嗣復曰：「古者任則不疑，齊桓公器管仲於讎虜，豈有倒持慮邪？」
units.en: Sifu replied, "In antiquity to appoint was to trust; Duke Huan of Qi prized Guan Zhong though he had been his enemy's captive—where is the worry about holding the sword backward?"
units.literal: Sifu said: "In antiquity, once a man was entrusted there was no doubting him; Duke Huan of Qi valued Guan Zhong though he had been a captive of his enemy—was there any thought of holding the sword reversed?"

units.zh: 帝以其面相觸，頗不悅。
units.en: The emperor, seeing them clash face to face, was deeply displeased.
units.literal: The emperor, because their faces clashed in debate, was quite displeased.

units.zh: 仙韶樂工尉遲璋授王府率，右拾遺竇洵直當衙論奏，鄭覃、嗣復嫌以細故，謂洵直近名。
units.en: The Xianshao musician Yuchi Zhang was made commandant of the princely household; Remonstrance Official Dou Xunzhi protested at court, but Zheng Tan and Sifu dismissed it as trivial and accused Xunzhi of seeking renown.
units.literal: A Xianshao musician, Yuchi Zhang, was appointed commandant of the princely household; Remonstrance Official Dou Xunzhi memorialized at court, and Zheng Tan and Sifu disliked it as a petty matter, saying Xunzhi was courting fame.

units.zh: 夷行曰：「諫官當衙，正須論宰相得失，彼賤工安足言者？
units.en: Yixing said, "Remonstrance officials at court ought to debate the chancellors' merits and faults—what business has a lowly musician in the matter?
units.literal: Yixing said: "When remonstrance officials attend court, they ought precisely to discuss the chancellors' right and wrong—what is that base artisan fit to speak of?

units.zh: 然亦不可置不用。」
units.en: Still, he should not simply be ignored."
units.literal: Yet he also cannot simply be set aside and unused."

units.zh: 帝即徙璋光州長史，以百縑賜洵直。
units.en: The emperor immediately reassigned Zhang as chief clerk of Guang Prefecture and rewarded Xunzhi with a hundred bolts of silk.
units.literal: The emperor at once transferred Zhang to be Chief Clerk of Guang Prefecture and gave Xunzhi a hundred bolts of silk.

units.zh: 進門下侍郎。
units.en: Yixing was promoted to vice director of the Chancellery.
units.literal: He was advanced to Vice Director of the Chancellery.

units.zh: 帝常怪天寶政事不善，問：「姚元崇、宋璟於時在否？」
units.en: The emperor often lamented the poor governance of the Tianbao years and asked, "Were Yao Chong and Song Jing still in office then?"
units.literal: The emperor often wondered at the poor governance of the Tianbao era and asked: "Were Yao Chong and Song Jing in office at that time?"

units.zh: 李玨曰：「姚亡而宋罷。」
units.en: Li Jue answered, "Yao was dead and Song had already been removed."
units.literal: Li Jue said: "Yao was dead and Song had been dismissed."

units.zh: 玨因推言：「玄宗自謂未嘗殺一不辜，而任李林甫，種夷數十族，不亦惑乎？」
units.en: Jue went on, "Xuanzong boasted that he had never killed an innocent man, yet he entrusted Li Linfu, who wiped out dozens of clans—was that not delusion?"
units.literal: Jue then extended the argument: "Xuanzong claimed he had never killed a single innocent man, yet he employed Li Linfu, who exterminated dozens of clans—was he not deluded?"

units.zh: 夷行曰：「陛下今亦宜戒以權屬人。」
units.en: Yixing said, "Your Majesty today should likewise beware of handing power to others."
units.literal: Yixing said: "Your Majesty today should also take warning against vesting authority in others."

units.zh: 嗣復曰：「夷行失言，太宗易暴亂為仁義，用房玄齡十有六年，任魏徵十有五年，未嘗失道。
units.en: Sifu said, "Yixing is wrong. Taizong turned chaos into humane rule; he kept Fang Xuanling for sixteen years and Wei Zheng for fifteen without ever losing his way.
units.literal: Sifu said: "Yixing has misspoken. Taizong transformed violence and disorder into benevolence and righteousness; he employed Fang Xuanling for sixteen years and Wei Zheng for fifteen, and never strayed from the right path.

units.zh: 人主用忠良久益治，用邪佞一日多矣。」
units.en: A ruler who keeps loyal men long grows more orderly; employ the wicked for a day and trouble multiplies."
units.literal: When a ruler employs the loyal for a long time, governance grows ever better; employ the wicked and fawning for a single day and harm multiplies."

units.zh: 時用郭薳為坊州刺史，右拾遺宋邧論不可，果坐贓敗。
units.en: Guo Fan had just been made prefect of Fangzhou; Remonstrance Official Song Fang objected, and Fan was later indeed convicted of corruption.
units.literal: At the time Guo Fan was appointed prefect of Fangzhou; Remonstrance Official Song Fang argued against it, and Fan was indeed later ruined on charges of corruption.

units.zh: 帝欲賞邧，夷行曰：「諫官論事是其職，若一事善輒進官，恐後不免有私。」
units.en: The emperor wanted to reward Fang; Yixing said, "Remonstrance is their duty; promote them for every good memorial and they will soon court favoritism."
units.literal: The emperor wished to reward Fang; Yixing said: "For remonstrance officials to discuss affairs is their duty; if every good act at once wins promotion, I fear that later they cannot avoid partiality."

units.zh: 夷行蓋專詆嗣復。
units.en: In truth Yixing was chiefly bent on attacking Sifu.
units.literal: Yixing was in fact devoted to slandering Sifu.

units.zh: 又素善覃，陰助其力，以排折朋黨。
units.en: He had always been close to Zheng Tan and quietly backed him in breaking up the factions.
units.literal: He had long been on good terms with Zheng Tan and secretly aided his strength to break up the factional cliques.

units.zh: 是時，雖天子亦惡其太過，恩禮遂衰，罷為吏部尚書，尋拜華州刺史。
units.en: By then even the emperor disliked his excesses; imperial favor waned, he was demoted to minister of personnel, and soon made prefect of Huazhou.
units.literal: At this time even the Son of Heaven disliked his excess; favor and ceremony declined, and he was removed to Minister of Personnel, then soon appointed prefect of Huazhou.

units.zh: 武宗即位，召為御史大夫，俄還門下侍郎平章事，進位尚書左仆射。
units.en: When Wuzong acceded, Yixing was recalled as censor-in-chief, soon restored as vice chancellor, and promoted to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Yixing was summoned as Censor-in-Chief; soon he returned as Vice Director of the Chancellery and Chief Minister, and was advanced to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 夷行與崔珙俱拜，乃奏：「仆射始視事，受四品官拜，無著令。
units.en: When Yixing and Cui Gong took office together, they submitted: "When a vice director begins his duties and receives bows from fourth-rank officials, no statute authorizes it.
units.literal: When Yixing and Cui Gong were both invested, they memorialized: "When a vice director first assumes office and receives the bows of fourth-rank officials, there is no established statute.

units.zh: 比日左右丞、吏部侍郎、御史中丞皆為仆射拜階下，謂之『隔品致敬』。
units.en: Lately the assistant directors, vice minister of personnel, and vice censor-in-chief have all bowed to the vice director on the lower steps—the so-called 'cross-rank salute.'
units.literal: Lately the left and right assistant directors, the vice minister of personnel, and the vice censor-in-chief have all bowed to the vice director on the steps below, which is called 'paying respect across ranks.'

units.zh: 準禮，皇太子見上臺群官，群官先拜而後答，以無二上也。
units.en: By ritual, when the crown prince meets senior officials, they bow first and he responds, for there cannot be two superiors.
units.literal: According to ritual, when the crown prince meets the senior officials of the upper terrace, the officials bow first and he then responds, because there cannot be two superiors.

units.zh: 仆射與四品官並列朝廷，不容獨優。
units.en: The vice director ranks with fourth-grade officials at court and must not be singled out for privilege.
units.literal: The vice director stands in court on a par with fourth-rank officials; he cannot be uniquely privileged.

units.zh: 前日鄭餘慶著《仆射上儀》，謂隔品官無亢禮。
units.en: Earlier Zheng Yuqing had written the Ceremonial for Vice Directors at Court, holding that officials of different rank owed no reciprocal salute.
units.literal: Formerly Zheng Yuqing compiled the Ceremonial for Vice Directors at Court and held that officials of separated rank owed no opposing salute.

units.zh: 時竇易直任御史中丞，議不可。
units.en: Dou Yizhi, then vice censor-in-chief, argued against it.
units.literal: At the time Dou Yizhi served as vice censor-in-chief and argued that this would not do.

units.zh: 及易直自為仆射，乃忘前議，當時鄙厭之。
units.en: When Yizhi himself became vice director, he forgot his earlier view, and contemporaries despised him for it.
units.literal: When Yizhi himself became vice director, he forgot his earlier argument, and people of the time despised him for it.

units.zh: 臣等不願以失禮速誚於時。
units.en: We do not wish to be swiftly reproached for breach of ritual.
units.literal: Your subjects do not wish to be quickly reproached by the age for breach of ritual.

units.zh: 且開元元年，以左右仆射為左右丞相，位次三公，三公上日答拜，而仆射受之，非是。
units.en: Moreover, in 713 the left and right vice directors were made chief ministers ranking after the Three Dukes; on the dukes' court days they returned bows while the vice directors merely received them—this was wrong.
units.literal: Moreover, in the first year of Kaiyuan the left and right vice directors were made left and right chief ministers, ranking after the Three Dukes; on the Three Dukes' court days they returned bows, yet the vice directors received them—this was not correct.

units.zh: 望敕所司約《三公上儀》，著定令。」
units.en: We ask that the relevant offices be ordered to follow the Ceremonial for the Three Dukes at Court and fix the rule in law."
units.literal: We hope Your Majesty will order the relevant offices to follow the Ceremonial for the Three Dukes at Court and fix it as statute."

units.zh: 詔可。
units.en: The edict approved the request.
units.literal: An edict approved.

units.zh: 始，累朝紛議不決，至夷行遂定。
units.en: For generations the court had debated without resolution; Yixing settled the matter.
units.literal: From the beginning successive courts had debated without resolution; with Yixing it was finally settled.

units.zh: 以足疾乞身，罷為太子太保，以檢校司空為河中節度使，卒。
units.en: Citing foot ailment he resigned, was made grand guardian of the heir apparent, then military commissioner of Hezhong with honorary minister of works, and died in office.
units.literal: He pleaded illness of the feet to retire, was removed to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, then served as military commissioner of Hezhong with the honorary title of Minister of Works, and died.

units.zh: 李紳，字公垂，中書令敬玄曾孫。
units.en: Li Shen, courtesy name Gongchui, was the great-grandson of Chief Minister Jingxuan.
units.literal: Li Shen, styled Gongchui, was the great-grandson of Chief Minister Jingxuan.

units.zh: 世宦南方，客潤州。
units.en: His family had served in the south for generations and lived as guests in Runzhou.
units.literal: For generations the family had held office in the south and sojourned in Runzhou.

units.zh: 紳六歲而孤，哀等成人。
units.en: Shen lost his father at six and grieved as deeply as an adult.
units.literal: Shen was orphaned at six and mourned with the grief of a grown man.

units.zh: 母盧，躬授之學。
units.en: His mother, née Lu, taught him herself.
units.literal: His mother, of the Lu clan, personally taught him.

units.zh: 為人短小精悍，於詩最有名，時號「短李」。
units.en: Short in stature but sharp and forceful, he was famed above all for poetry and was known as 'Short Li.'
units.literal: In person he was short, keen, and vigorous; in poetry he was most renowned, and people of the time called him 'Short Li.'

units.zh: 蘇州刺史韋夏卿數稱之。
units.en: Wei Xiaqing, prefect of Suzhou, often praised him.
units.literal: Wei Xiaqing, prefect of Suzhou, repeatedly praised him.

units.zh: 葬母，有烏銜芝墜輔車。
units.en: At his mother's burial a crow dropped a piece of lingzhi fungus onto the hearse.
units.literal: When he buried his mother, a crow carrying fungus dropped it onto the funeral carriage.

units.zh: 元和初，擢進士第，補國子助教，不樂，輒去。
units.en: Early in the Yuanhe reign he passed the jinshi examination and was made an assistant instructor at the Imperial University, but he was unhappy and soon resigned.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant instructor at the Imperial University; discontented, he soon left.

units.zh: 客金陵，李锜愛其才，辟掌書記。
units.en: While staying in Jinling he was recruited by Li Qi, who admired his talent, as chief secretary.
units.literal: Sojourning in Jinling, Li Qi admired his talent and recruited him as chief secretary.

units.zh: 锜浸不法，賓客莫敢言，紳數諫，不入；
units.en: Qi grew lawless; none of his staff dared speak up, though Shen admonished him again and again to no effect;
units.literal: Qi grew increasingly lawless; none of his retainers dared speak, but Shen remonstrated repeatedly without being heeded;

units.zh: 欲去，不許。
units.en: he tried to leave but was not allowed.
units.literal: he wished to leave but was not permitted.

units.zh: 會使者召锜，稱疾，留後王淡為具行，锜怒，陰教士臠食之，即脅使者為眾奏天子，幸得留。
units.en: When an imperial envoy summoned Qi to court, Qi feigned illness and had the acting commissioner Wang Dan prepare to go in his place; enraged, Qi secretly had soldiers dismember and eat Dan, then forced the envoy to petition the throne in the troops' name and was allowed to stay.
units.literal: It happened that an envoy summoned Qi; Qi claimed illness and had the acting commissioner Wang Dan prepare for departure. Qi was enraged, secretly ordered soldiers to cut Dan to pieces and eat him, then coerced the envoy to report to the Son of Heaven on behalf of the troops, and by good fortune was allowed to remain.

units.zh: 锜召紳作疏，坐锜前，紳陽怖栗，至不能為字，下筆輒塗去，盡數紙。
units.en: Qi ordered Shen to draft the memorial and sat him before him; Shen pretended to tremble with fear until he could not write a word, smearing out every stroke until several sheets were ruined.
units.literal: Qi summoned Shen to draft a memorial and seated him before himself; Shen feigned terror until he could not form a character, and whenever he put brush to paper he at once smeared it away, using up several sheets.

units.zh: 锜怒罵曰：「何敢爾，不憚死邪？」
units.en: Qi raged and shouted, "How dare you—are you not afraid to die?"
units.literal: Qi raged and cursed: "How dare you act thus—are you not afraid of death?"

units.zh: 對曰：「生未嘗見金革，今得死為幸。」
units.en: He answered, "I have never known war; to die now would be a blessing."
units.literal: He replied: "In life I have never seen arms and armor; to die now would be my good fortune."

units.zh: 即註以刃，令易紙，復然。
units.en: Qi pressed a blade to him and ordered fresh paper; Shen did the same again.
units.literal: Qi at once pressed a blade to him and ordered fresh paper; Shen did the same again.

units.zh: 或言許縱能軍中書，紳不足用。
units.en: Someone said Xu Zong could write the needed document and that Shen was useless.
units.literal: Someone said Xu Zong could write military documents and that Shen was of no use.

units.zh: 召縱至，操書如所欲，即囚紳獄中，锜誅，乃免。
units.en: Zong was summoned, wrote as required, and Shen was thrown into prison; he was freed only when Qi was executed.
units.literal: Zong was summoned; he wrote as desired, and Shen was at once imprisoned; when Qi was executed, Shen was released.

units.zh: 或欲以聞，謝曰：「本激於義，非市名也。」
units.en: Some wanted to report his conduct to the court; he refused, saying, "I acted from duty, not to buy a reputation."
units.literal: Some wished to report this to the court; he declined, saying: "I was moved by righteousness, not trading on fame."

units.zh: 乃止。
units.en: So they let the matter drop.
units.literal: And so they desisted.

units.zh: 久之，從辟山南觀察府。
units.en: After some time he entered the staff of the Shannan observation commission.
units.literal: After a long while he followed a summons to the Shannan observation commission.

units.zh: 穆宗召為右拾遺、翰林學士，與李德裕、元稹同時，號「三俊」。
units.en: Muzong made him right remonstrance official and Hanlin academician; with Li Deyu and Yuan Zhen he was called one of the 'Three Talents.'
units.literal: Emperor Muzong summoned him as Right Remonstrance Official and Hanlin academician; together with Li Deyu and Yuan Zhen at the same time, they were styled the 'Three Talents.'

units.zh: 累擢中書舍人。
units.en: He rose to secretariat drafter.
units.literal: He was promoted in succession to Secretariat Drafter.

units.zh: 稹為宰相，而李逢吉教人告於方事，稹遂罷；
units.en: When Zhen became chief minister, Li Fengji engineered an accusation in the Yu Fang affair and had him dismissed;
units.literal: Zhen became chief minister, but Li Fengji had someone accuse him in the Yu Fang affair, and Zhen was removed;

units.zh: 欲引牛僧孺，懼紳等在禁近沮解，乃授德裕浙西觀察使。
units.en: wishing to bring in Niu Sengru, he feared Shen and others near the throne would block him, and sent Deyu to Zhexi as observation commissioner.
units.literal: Fengji wished to bring in Niu Sengru and, fearing that Shen and others in close attendance at court would obstruct the plan, appointed Deyu observation commissioner of Zhexi.

units.zh: 僧孺輔政，以紳為御史中丞，顧其氣剛卞，易疵累，而韓愈勁直，乃以愈為京兆尹，兼御史大夫，免臺參以激紳。
units.en: When Sengru took power he made Shen vice censor-in-chief, counting on his stiff temper to invite mistakes; he paired him with the blunt Han Yu as metropolitan prefect and concurrent censor-in-chief, exempting Yu from censorate attendance to provoke Shen.
units.literal: When Sengru held power, he made Shen vice censor-in-chief, considering his temperament stern and unyielding and easy to fault; Han Yu was forceful and upright, so Yu was made metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and concurrently censor-in-chief, exempted from censorate attendance to provoke Shen.

units.zh: 紳、愈果不相下，更持臺府故事，論詰往反，詆訐紛然，繇是皆罷之，以紳為江西觀察使。
units.en: Shen and Han Yu would not yield; they traded censorate precedents in endless dispute until both were dismissed, and Shen was sent to Jiangxi as observation commissioner.
units.literal: Shen and Yu indeed would not yield to each other; they cited censorate precedents back and forth in mutual accusation until slander filled the air; for this both were removed, and Shen was made observation commissioner of Jiangxi.

units.zh: 帝素厚遇紳，遣使者就第勞賜，以為樂外遷，紳泣言為逢吉中傷。
units.en: The emperor, who had always favored Shen, sent messengers to his home with gifts, assuming he welcomed the provincial post; Shen wept and said Fengji had slandered him.
units.literal: The emperor had always treated Shen generously and sent an envoy to his residence to console and reward him, thinking he was pleased with an outside appointment; Shen wept and said he had been slandered by Fengji.

units.zh: 入謝，又自陳所以然，帝悟，改戶部侍郎。
units.en: At his audience of thanks he explained everything again; the emperor understood and made him vice minister of revenue.
units.literal: When he came to give thanks he again explained the reason himself; the emperor understood and changed his appointment to Vice Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 逢吉終欲陷之。
units.en: Fengji still meant to destroy him.
units.literal: Fengji in the end still wished to entrap him.

units.zh: 紳族子虞，有文學名，隱居華陽，自言不願仕，時來省紳，雅與柏耆、程昔範善。
units.en: Shen's kinsman Yu was known for letters, lived in seclusion at Huayang, claimed he would not take office, visited Shen from time to time, and was close to Bai Qi and Cheng Xifan.
units.literal: Shen's clansman Yu had a literary reputation, lived in seclusion at Huayang, and declared he did not wish to serve; he would visit Shen from time to time and was on good terms with Bai Qi and Cheng Xifan.

units.zh: 及耆為拾遺，虞以書求薦，紳惡其無立操，痛誚之。
units.en: When Qi became remonstrance official, Yu wrote asking Shen to recommend him; Shen despised his lack of principle and rebuked him harshly.
units.literal: When Qi became remonstrance official, Yu wrote asking for recommendation; Shen detested his lack of firm principle and rebuked him sharply.

units.zh: 虞失望，後至京師，悉暴紳所言於逢吉。
units.en: Disappointed, Yu later came to the capital and repeated everything Shen had said to Fengji.
units.literal: Yu was disappointed; later he came to the capital and fully exposed everything Shen had said to Fengji.

units.zh: 逢吉滋怒，乃用張又新、李續等計，擢虞、昔範與劉棲楚皆為拾遺，以伺紳隙，內結中人王守澄自助。
units.en: Fengji, enraged, followed the counsel of Zhang Youxin and Li Xu, promoting Yu, Xifan, and Liu Qichu as remonstrance officials to spy on Shen while secretly winning the eunuch Wang Shoucheng.
units.literal: Fengji grew still angrier and adopted the plan of Zhang Youxin, Li Xu, and others, promoting Yu, Xifan, and Liu Qichu all to remonstrance officials to watch for openings against Shen, while secretly allying with the eunuch Wang Shoucheng for support.

units.zh: 會敬宗立，逢吉知紳失勢可乘，使守澄從容奏言：「先帝始議立太子，杜元穎、李紳勸立深王，獨宰相逢吉請立陛下，而李續、李虞助之。」
units.en: When Jingzong succeeded, Fengji saw Shen was vulnerable and had Shoucheng report calmly: "When the late emperor first debated the heir, Du Yuanying and Li Shen favored Prince Shen; only Chief Minister Fengji urged installing Your Majesty, aided by Li Xu and Li Yu."
units.literal: When Emperor Jingzong acceded, Fengji knew Shen had lost power and could be struck; he had Shoucheng calmly report: "When the late emperor first discussed establishing the heir, Du Yuanying and Li Shen urged installing Prince Shen; only Chief Minister Fengji asked to install Your Majesty, and Li Xu and Li Yu assisted him."

units.zh: 逢吉乘間言紳嘗不利於陛下，請逐之。
units.en: Fengji then said Shen had once opposed the emperor and asked that he be banished.
units.literal: Fengji seized the moment to say Shen had once been unfavorable to Your Majesty and asked that he be expelled.

units.zh: 帝初即位，不能辨，乃貶紳為端州司馬。
units.en: The new emperor could not tell truth from slander and demoted Shen to military adjutant of Duanzhou.
units.literal: The emperor had just taken the throne and could not discern the truth, so Shen was demoted to military adjutant of Duanzhou.

units.zh: 棲楚等怒得善地，皆切齒。
units.en: Qichu and his allies, furious that Shen had received so mild a posting, gnashed their teeth.
units.literal: Qichu and the others, angry that he had received so mild a place, all gnashed their teeth.

units.zh: 詔下，百官賀逢吉，唯右拾遺吳思不往，逢吉斥思，令告大行喪於吐蕃。
units.en: When the edict appeared, the officials congratulated Fengji—all except Right Remonstrance Official Wu Si, whom Fengji banished to announce the late emperor's mourning in Tibet.
units.literal: When the edict was issued, all officials congratulated Fengji; only Right Remonstrance Official Wu Si did not go. Fengji expelled Si and ordered him to announce the late emperor's mourning in Tibet.

units.zh: 此時，人無敢言者，惟韋處厚屢言紳枉，折逢吉之奸。
units.en: No one dared speak then except Wei Chuhou, who repeatedly declared Shen's innocence and exposed Fengji's malice.
units.literal: At this time no one dared speak; only Wei Chuhou repeatedly said Shen had been wronged and rebutted Fengji's treachery.

units.zh: 後天子於禁中得先帝手緘書一笥，發之，見裴度、元穎、紳三疏請立帝為嗣，始大感悟，悉焚逢吉黨所上謗書。
units.en: Later the emperor found in the palace a box of the late emperor's sealed papers; inside were memorials by Pei Du, Yuan Ying, and Shen urging his installation as heir. Greatly enlightened, he burned every slanderous document from Fengji's faction.
units.literal: Later the Son of Heaven obtained in the palace a case of the late emperor's own sealed writings; opening it, he saw three memorials by Pei Du, Yuan Ying, and Shen asking to establish him as heir, and was greatly enlightened; he burned all the slanderous documents submitted by Fengji's faction.

units.zh: 始，紳南逐，歷封、康間，湍瀨險澀，惟乘漲流乃濟。
units.en: When Shen was first exiled south, the rapids between Feng and Kang were so dangerous that only a flood tide made passage possible.
units.literal: At first, as Shen was driven south, he passed between Feng and Kang; the rapids were perilous and treacherous, and only by riding the flood tide could he cross.

units.zh: 康州有媼龍祠，舊傳能致雲雨，紳以書禱，俄而大漲。
units.en: At Kangzhou stood the Old Dragon Shrine, said to summon rain; Shen prayed there in writing, and the river soon swelled.
units.literal: Kangzhou had the Old Dragon Shrine, traditionally said to bring clouds and rain; Shen prayed there in writing, and soon the waters rose greatly.

units.zh: 寶歷赦令不言左降官與量移，處厚執爭，詔為追定，得徙江州長史，遷滁、壽二州刺史。
units.en: The Baoli amnesty omitted demoted officials eligible for graduated transfer; Chuhou protested until an edict amended it, and Shen was moved to serve as Chief Clerk of Jiang Prefecture, then made prefect of Chu and Shou Prefectures.
units.literal: The Baoli amnesty did not mention demoted officials or graduated transfers; Chuhou argued firmly, and an edict was issued to amend it, allowing Shen to become Chief Clerk of Jiang Prefecture and then prefect of Chu and Shou Prefectures.

units.zh: 霍山多虎，擷茶者病之，治機阱，發民跡射，不能止。
units.en: Huoshan had many tigers that plagued tea pickers; traps were set and the people sent to hunt them, without success.
units.literal: Huoshan had many tigers; tea pickers suffered from them; traps were set and the people were sent to track and shoot them, but they could not be stopped.

units.zh: 紳至，盡去之，虎不為暴。
units.en: When Shen arrived he had the traps removed, and the tigers ceased their depredations.
units.literal: When Shen arrived, he had them all removed, and the tigers no longer ravaged.

units.zh: 以太子賓客分司東都。
units.en: He served as guest of the heir apparent at the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: He served as Guest of the Heir Apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital.

units.zh: 太和中，李德裕當國，擢紳浙東觀察使。
units.en: During the Taihe reign, with Li Deyu in power, Shen was made observation commissioner of Zhedong.
units.literal: In the Taihe era, when Li Deyu held power, Shen was promoted to observation commissioner of Zhedong.

units.zh: 李宗閔方得君，復以太子賓客分司。
units.en: When Li Zongmin gained the emperor's ear, Shen was again made guest of the heir apparent at the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: When Li Zongmin had just won the emperor's favor, Shen was again made Guest of the Heir Apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital.

units.zh: 開成初，鄭覃以紳為河南尹。
units.en: Early in the Kaicheng reign, Zheng Tan made him metropolitan prefect of Henan.
units.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng, Zheng Tan appointed Shen metropolitan prefect of Henan.

units.zh: 河南多惡少，或危帽散衣，擊大毯，屍官道，車馬不敢前。
units.en: Henan teemed with hoodlums who wore outlandish dress, beat huge drums, and sprawled across the highway until traffic dared not pass.
units.literal: Henan had many rowdies; some wore tall hats and loose clothes, struck great drums, and lay corpse-like across the official road so that carriages and horses dared not advance.

units.zh: 紳治剛嚴，皆望風遁去。
units.en: Shen ruled with iron discipline, and they fled at his approach.
units.literal: Shen governed with stern rigor, and all fled at the sight of him.

units.zh: 遷宣武節度使。
units.en: He was transferred to military commissioner of Xuanwu.
units.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner of Xuanwu.

units.zh: 大旱，蝗不入境。
units.en: Though drought struck the region, locusts did not cross his border.
units.literal: There was great drought, but locusts did not enter his territory.

units.zh: 武宗即位，徙淮南，召拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，進尚書右仆射、門下侍郎，封趙郡公。
units.en: When Wuzong succeeded, Shen was shifted to Huainan, then recalled as vice director of the Secretariat and chief minister, promoted to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and vice chancellor, and created Duke of Zhao.
units.literal: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Shen was moved to Huainan, then summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Director of the Chancellery, advanced to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Director of the Chancellery, and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao commandery.

units.zh: 居位四年，以足緩不任朝謁，辭位，以檢校右仆射平章事，復節度淮南。
units.en: After four years in office his feet failed him for court attendance; he resigned, took honorary rank as right vice director and chief minister, and returned to command Huainan.
units.literal: After four years in office, his feet being slow and unable to bear court attendance, he resigned his post and served as honorary right vice director with chief ministerial rank, again commanding Huainan.

units.zh: 卒，贈太尉，謚文肅。
units.en: He died and was posthumously made grand commandant with the posthumous title Wensu.
units.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Grand Commandant and given the posthumous title Wensu.

units.zh: 始，灃人吳汝納者，韶州刺史武陵兄子也。
units.en: This concerns Wu Runa of Feng, nephew of Wuling, prefect of Shaozhou.
units.literal: At the beginning, there was Wu Runa of Feng, nephew of Wuling, prefect of Shaozhou.

units.zh: 武陵坐贓貶潘州司戶參軍死，汝納家被逐，久不調。
units.en: Wuling was demoted for corruption to Panzhou as army adjutant and died there; Runa's family was exiled and he long went without office.
units.literal: Wuling was demoted for corruption to army adjutant of Panzhou and died there; Runa's family was driven out and long went without appointment.

units.zh: 時李吉甫任宰相，汝納怨之，後遂附宗閔黨中。
units.en: Li Jifu was then chief minister; Runa bore him a grudge and later joined Li Zongmin's faction.
units.literal: At the time Li Jifu held the chancellorship; Runa resented him and later attached himself to Li Zongmin's faction.

units.zh: 會昌時，為永寧尉，弟湘為江都尉。
units.en: During the Huichang reign he was captain of Yongning; his brother Xiang was captain of Jiangdu.
units.literal: In the Huichang era he was captain of Yongning; his younger brother Xiang was captain of Jiangdu.

units.zh: 部人訟湘受贓狼籍，身娶民顏悅女。
units.en: People in the district accused Xiang of rampant corruption and of marrying the daughter of Yan Yue, a commoner.
units.literal: People of the district sued Xiang for corruption in heaps, and that he had personally married the daughter of a commoner, Yan Yue.

units.zh: 紳使觀察判官魏铏鞫湘，罪明白，論報殺之。
units.en: Shen had Wei Xing, judicial reviewer for the observation commission, interrogate Xiang. His guilt was clearly established, and Xiang was sentenced to death.
units.literal: Shen had Wei Xing, judicial reviewer for the observation commission, interrogate Xiang; his guilt was clearly established, and Xiang was sentenced to death.

units.zh: 時，議者謂吳氏世與宰相有嫌，疑紳內顧望，織成其罪。
units.en: Commentators said the Wu family had long feuded with chief ministers and suspected Shen of bias in fabricating the case.
units.literal: At the time commentators said the Wu clan had long borne grudges against chief ministers and suspected Shen of inward partiality, fabricating the crime.

units.zh: 諫官屢論列，詔遣御史崔元藻覆按，元藻言湘盜用程糧錢有狀，娶部人女不實，按悅嘗為青州衙推，而妻王故衣冠女，不應坐。
units.en: Remonstrance officials protested repeatedly until Censor Cui Yuanzao was sent to reinvestigate; he found Xiang had misused transport funds, that the charge of marrying a commoner's daughter was false—Yue had been a Qingzhou yamen officer and his wife Wang came from an official family and was not liable.
units.literal: Remonstrance officials repeatedly argued the case; an edict sent Investigating Censor Cui Yuanzao to reinvestigate. Yuanzao said Xiang had indeed misappropriated transport-grain funds, that marrying a district woman's daughter was untrue—investigation showed Yue had once been yamen push of Qingzhou and his wife Wang was a woman of an old official family and should not be implicated.

units.zh: 德裕惡元藻持兩端，奏貶崖州司戶參軍。
units.en: Deyu despised Yuanzao's wavering and had him demoted to army adjutant of Yazhou.
units.literal: Deyu detested Yuanzao's fence-sitting and memorialized to demote him to army adjutant of Yazhou.

units.zh: 宣宗立，德裕去位，紳已卒。
units.en: When Xuanzong succeeded, Deyu fell from power and Shen was already dead.
units.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, Deyu left office and Shen was already dead.

units.zh: 崔鉉等久不得誌，導汝納使為湘訟，言：「湘素直，為人誣蔑，大校重牢，五木被體，吏至以娶妻資媵結贓。」
units.en: Cui Xuan and others, long thwarted, coached Runa to sue for Xiang, claiming: "Xiang was upright but slandered; he was thrown into a commander's dungeon, tortured with the five punishments, and officials even counted his bride-price as stolen goods."
units.literal: Cui Xuan and others had long been unable to satisfy their resentment and guided Runa to sue on Xiang's behalf, saying: "Xiang was by nature upright and was slandered by others; he was put in a major commander's heavy prison, the five punishments applied to his body, and officials even fabricated bribery by counting his bride-price and dowry as stolen goods."

units.zh: 且言：「顏悅故士族，湘罪皆不當死，紳枉殺之。」
units.en: They also said: "Yan Yue was of gentry stock; none of Xiang's offenses warranted death; Shen murdered him unjustly."
units.literal: They also said: "Yan Yue was of an old gentry family; none of Xiang's offenses warranted death; Shen killed him unjustly."

units.zh: 又言：「湘死，紳令即瘞，不得歸葬。
units.en: They also said: "When Xiang died, Shen had him buried at once and forbade return for proper interment.
units.literal: They further said: "When Xiang died, Shen ordered immediate burial and would not allow return for proper interment.

units.zh: 按紳以舊宰相鎮一方，恣威權。
units.en: Shen, a former chief minister ruling a circuit, had abused his power.
units.literal: Shen, as a former chief minister commanding a region, had wielded power arbitrarily.

units.zh: 凡戮有罪，猶待秋分；
units.en: Even for the guilty, executions normally wait until the autumn equinox;
units.literal: Whenever executing the guilty, one still waits for the autumn equinox;

units.zh: 湘無辜，盛夏被殺。」
units.en: yet innocent Xiang was killed in midsummer."
units.literal: Xiang was innocent yet was killed in the height of summer."

units.zh: 崔元藻銜德裕斥己，即翻其辭，因言：「御史覆獄還，皆對天子別白是非，德裕權軋天下，使不得對，具獄不付有司，但用紳奏而寘湘死。」
units.en: Cui Yuanzao, bitter at Deyu's demotion of him, reversed his story and said: "When censors return from reinvestigating cases they report findings directly to the emperor, but Deyu blocked this, withheld the full dossier from the courts, and relied solely on Shen's memorial to execute Xiang."
units.literal: Cui Yuanzao, resenting Deyu's dismissal of him, at once reversed his testimony and said: "When censors return from reinvestigating cases they all explain right and wrong separately to the Son of Heaven; Deyu's power crushed the realm so they could not report; the full record was not given to the authorities—only Shen's memorial was used to put Xiang to death."

units.zh: 是時，德裕已失權，而宗閔故黨令狐、崔鉉、白敏中皆當路，因是逞憾，以利誘動元藻等，使三司結紳杖鉞作藩，虐殺良平，準神龍詔書，酷吏歿者官爵皆奪，子孫不得進宦，紳雖亡，請從《春秋》戮死者之比。
units.en: Deyu was already out of power, but Zongmin's allies Linghu, Cui Xuan, and Bai Minzhong controlled the government; they vented old grudges, bribed Yuanzao to change his story, and had the Three Offices find that Shen, as a frontier commissioner wielding the axe, had murdered the innocent; citing the Shenlong edict stripping dead cruel officials and barring their descendants, they demanded posthumous punishment of Shen under the Spring and Autumn precedent.
units.literal: By then Deyu had lost power, while Zongmin's old associates Linghu, Cui Xuan, and Bai Minzhong all held the road; they vented their resentment, enticing Yuanzao and others with profit, and had the Three Offices conclude that Shen, bearing the axe as a frontier commander, had cruelly killed the innocent; according to the Shenlong edict, dead cruel officials had rank and titles stripped and descendants barred from office—though Shen was dead, they asked to apply the Spring and Autumn Annals' analogy for posthumous punishment.

units.zh: 詔削紳三官，子孫不得仕。
units.en: An edict stripped three ranks from Shen and barred his descendants from office.
units.literal: An edict stripped three ranks from Shen and barred his descendants from office.

units.zh: 貶德裕等，擢汝納左拾遺，元藻武功令。
units.en: Deyu and others were demoted; Runa was made left remonstrance official and Yuanzao magistrate of Wugong.
units.literal: Deyu and others were demoted; Runa was promoted to Left Remonstrance Official and Yuanzao to magistrate of Wugong.

units.zh: 始，紳以文藝節操見用，而屢為怨仇所拫卻，卒能自伸其才，以名位終。
units.en: Shen had risen on literary talent and integrity, was repeatedly struck down by enemies, yet in the end fulfilled his gifts and died with rank and renown.
units.literal: At the beginning, Shen was employed for literary talent and integrity, yet was repeatedly struck down by enemies; in the end he was able to extend his abilities and ended with fame and rank.

units.zh: 所至務為威烈，或陷暴刻，故雖沒而坐湘冤雲。
units.en: Everywhere he went he ruled with fierce severity, sometimes to the point of cruelty; hence even after death the injustice of Xiang's case clung to his name.
units.literal: Wherever he went he strove for stern authority, and sometimes fell into harsh severity; therefore even after death he bore the cloud of Xiang's wrongful case.

units.zh: 李讓夷，字達心，系本隴西。
units.en: Li Rangyi, courtesy name Daxin, was of Longxi descent.
units.literal: Li Rangyi, styled Daxin, traced his lineage to Longxi.

units.zh: 擢進士第，辟鎮國李絳府判官。
units.en: After passing the jinshi examination he joined Li Jiang's Zhenguo staff as administrative aide.
units.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was recruited as administrative aide in Li Jiang's Zhenguo headquarters.

units.zh: 又從西川杜元穎幕府。
units.en: He later served on Du Yuanying's staff in western Sichuan.
units.literal: He also followed Du Yuanying's western Sichuan headquarters.

units.zh: 與宋申錫善，申錫為翰林學士，薦讓夷右拾遺，俄召拜學士。
units.en: Close to Song Shenxi, he was recommended by Shenxi as right remonstrance official when Shenxi entered the Hanlin Academy, and soon became a Hanlin academician himself.
units.literal: He was on good terms with Song Shenxi; when Shenxi became Hanlin academician he recommended Rangyi as Right Remonstrance Official, and soon Rangyi was summoned as academician.

units.zh: 素善薛廷老，廷老不飭細檢，數飲酒不治職，罷去，坐是亦奪職。
units.en: He was also close to Xue Tinglao, who was lax in conduct, often drank on duty, and was dismissed; Rangyi lost his post for the association.
units.literal: He had long been friendly with Xue Tinglao; Tinglao did not discipline himself in small matters, often drank and neglected duty, and was removed—for this Rangyi too was stripped of office.

units.zh: 累進諫議大夫。
units.en: He rose to remonstrance grandee.
units.literal: He was promoted in succession to Remonstrance Grandee.

units.zh: 開成初，起居舍人李褒免，文宗謂李石曰：「褚遂良以諫議大夫兼起居郎，今諫議誰歟？
units.en: Early in Kaicheng, diary attendant Li Bao was dismissed; Wenzong asked Li Shi, "Chu Suiliang once combined remonstrance grandee with diary attendant—who holds that remonstrance post now?
units.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng, Attendant of the Imperial Diary Li Bao was dismissed; Emperor Wenzong said to Li Shi: "Chu Suiliang served as remonstrance grandee concurrently as diary attendant—who holds remonstrance grandee now?

units.zh: 可言其人。」
units.en: Name a suitable candidate."
units.literal: Name someone suitable."

units.zh: 石以馮定、孫簡、蕭俶、李讓夷對，帝曰：「讓夷可也。」
units.en: Shi named Feng Ding, Sun Jian, Xiao Chu, and Li Rangyi; the emperor said, "Rangyi will do."
units.literal: Shi named Feng Ding, Sun Jian, Xiao Chu, and Li Rangyi; the emperor said: "Rangyi will do."

units.zh: 李固言請用崔球、張次宗。
units.en: Li Guyan urged Cui Qiu and Zhang Cizong instead.
units.literal: Li Guyan asked to use Cui Qiu and Zhang Cizong.

units.zh: 鄭覃曰：「球故與李宗閔善，且記註操筆在赤墀下，所書為後世法，不可用黨人。
units.en: Zheng Tan said, "Qiu was close to Li Zongmin, and the diary is written on the red steps as a model for posterity—a faction man must not hold it.
units.literal: Zheng Tan said: "Qiu was formerly close to Li Zongmin, and the diary record is written with brush below the red steps—what is written becomes law for later ages; a faction man cannot be used.

units.zh: 若裴中孺、李讓夷，臣不敢有言。」
units.en: As for Pei Zhongru and Li Rangyi, I have no objection."
units.literal: As for Pei Zhongru and Li Rangyi, your subject dares raise no objection."

units.zh: 乃決用讓夷，進中書舍人。
units.en: Rangyi was appointed and promoted to secretariat drafter.
units.literal: Rangyi was then chosen and promoted to Secretariat Drafter.

units.zh: 既而李玨、楊嗣復以覃之薦，終帝世不得遷。
units.en: Afterward, because Zheng Tan had recommended him, Li Jue and Yang Sifu kept Rangyi from further promotion for the rest of Wenzong's reign.
units.literal: Afterward, because Zheng Tan had recommended him, Li Jue and Yang Sifu kept Rangyi from promotion for the rest of the emperor's reign.

units.zh: 武宗初，李德裕復入，三遷至尚書右丞，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
units.en: Early in Wuzong's reign Li Deyu returned; after three promotions he became right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, then vice chancellor.
units.literal: At the beginning of Wuzong's reign Li Deyu returned to power; after three promotions he reached Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Director of the Chancellery.

units.zh: 潞州平，檢校尚書右仆射。
units.en: After the pacification of Luzhou he was made honorary right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: When Luzhou was pacified, he was made honorary Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 宣宗立，進司空、門下侍郎，為大行山陵使。
units.en: When Xuanzong succeeded, he was made minister of works and vice chancellor and appointed commissioner for the late emperor's tomb.
units.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, Rangyi was advanced to Minister of Works and Vice Director of the Chancellery and made commissioner for the late emperor's mausoleum.

units.zh: 未復土，拜淮南節度使。
units.en: Before the tomb was closed he was made military commissioner of Huainan.
units.literal: Before the earth was returned over the tomb, he was appointed military commissioner of Huainan.

units.zh: 以疾願還，卒於道，贈司徒。
units.en: Illness forced him to turn back; he died on the road and was posthumously made minister of education.
units.literal: Ill, he asked to return and died on the road; posthumously he was made Minister of Education.

units.zh: 讓夷廉介不妄交，位雖顯劇，以儉約自將，為世咨美。
units.en: Rangyi was upright and cautious in friendship; though his posts were weighty, he lived frugally and was widely admired.
units.literal: Rangyi was upright and did not associate lightly; though his position was eminent and demanding, he restrained himself with frugality, and the age praised him.

units.zh: 曹確，字剛中，河南河南人。
units.en: Cao Que, courtesy name Gangzhong, was from Henan in Henan circuit.
units.literal: Cao Que, styled Gangzhong, was a native of Henan in Henan circuit.

units.zh: 擢進士第，歷踐中外官，累拜兵部侍郎。
units.en: After passing the jinshi he served in central and provincial posts and rose to vice minister of war.
units.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, served in succession in central and local posts, and was repeatedly appointed Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 懿宗咸通中，以本官同中書門下平章事，俄進中書侍郎。
units.en: Under Yizong in the Xiantong era he became chief minister from his present rank and soon vice director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: In the Xiantong era of Emperor Yizong he was made Co-Director of the Chancellery from his present post and soon advanced to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 確邃儒術，器識方重，動循法度。
units.en: Que was deeply learned, grave in judgment, and scrupulous in following the law.
units.literal: Que was steeped in Confucian learning, his capacity and judgment square and weighty, and in action he followed the law.

units.zh: 時帝薄於德，昵寵優人李可及。
units.en: The emperor was weak in virtue and doted on the actor Li Keji.
units.literal: The emperor at the time was shallow in virtue and fondly favored the actor Li Keji.

units.zh: 可及者，能新聲，自度曲，辭調悽折，京師俞薄少年爭慕之，號為「拍彈」。
units.en: Keji composed new music with mournful lyrics; frivolous youths in the capital idolized him and called his style 'strumming and plucking.'
units.literal: Keji could produce new music, composed his own tunes, and his lyrics were plaintive and piercing; the frivolous youth of the capital all competed to admire him and called his art 'strumming and plucking.'

units.zh: 同昌公主喪畢，帝與郭淑妃悼念不已，可及為帝造曲，曰《嘆百年》，教舞者數百，皆珠翠襐飾，刻畫魚龍地衣，度用繒五千，倚曲作辭，哀思裴回，聞者皆涕下。
units.en: After Princess Tongchang's mourning ended, the emperor and Consort Guo could not cease grieving; Keji composed 'Lament for a Century' for hundreds of dancers in jeweled dress on carved dragon-and-fish carpets, using five thousand bolts of silk; the mournful lyrics moved all who heard them to tears.
units.literal: When Princess Tongchang's mourning was complete, the emperor and Consort Guo Shufei could not cease their grief; Keji composed for the emperor a piece called 'Lament for a Century,' taught several hundred dancers all adorned in pearls and kingfisher feathers, with dragon-and-fish carpets carved in relief; five thousand bolts of silk were used; lyrics were set to the tune, grief lingering and turning—all who heard wept.

units.zh: 舞闋，珠寶覆地，帝以為天下之至悲，愈寵之。
units.en: When the dance ended pearls and gems littered the floor; the emperor called it the deepest sorrow imaginable and favored Keji all the more.
units.literal: When the dance ended, pearls and gems covered the ground; the emperor thought it the utmost grief under heaven and favored Keji still more.

units.zh: 家嘗娶婦，帝曰：「第去，吾當賜酒。」
units.en: When a wedding was being celebrated in his household, the emperor said, "Go home; I will send wine."
units.literal: When his household was marrying a bride, the emperor said: "Go on home—I shall send wine."

units.zh: 俄而使者負二銀珰與之，皆珠珍也。
units.en: Soon messengers arrived bearing two silver flasks filled with pearls and gems.
units.literal: Soon envoys came bearing two silver flasks for him, all filled with pearls and treasures.

units.zh: 可及憑恩橫甚，人無敢斥，遂擢為威衛將軍。
units.en: Keji grew insolent on imperial favor; no one dared criticize him, and he was made a guard general.
units.literal: Keji, relying on favor, was extremely overbearing; no one dared reprove him, and he was promoted to general of the Guard of Awesome Majesty.

units.zh: 確曰：「太宗著令，文武官六百四十三，謂房玄齡曰：『朕設此待天下賢士。
units.en: Que said, "Taizong fixed six hundred forty-three civil and military posts and told Fang Xuanling, 'These are for the worthy of the realm.
units.literal: Que said: "Taizong issued regulations: six hundred forty-three civil and military offices. He told Fang Xuanling: 'I established these to await the worthy men of the realm.

units.zh: 工商雜流，假使技出等夷，正當厚給以財，不可假以官，與賢者比肩立、同坐食也。』
units.en: Merchants and artisans, however skilled, should be paid generously, not given office to stand and dine beside the worthy.'
units.literal: Merchants, artisans, and miscellaneous classes—even if their skill surpassed their peers, they should properly be richly rewarded with wealth, not lent office to stand shoulder to shoulder and eat at the same table with the worthy.'

units.zh: 文宗欲以樂工尉遲璋為王府率，拾遺竇洵直固爭，卒授光州長史。
units.en: Wenzong wanted the musician Yuchi Zhang as princely commandant; Remonstrance Official Dou Xunzhi protested until Zhang was sent to serve as Chief Clerk of Guang Prefecture.
units.literal: Wenzong wished to make the musician Yuchi Zhang commandant of the princely household; Remonstrance Official Dou Xunzhi firmly protested, and Zhang was finally appointed Chief Clerk of Guang Prefecture.

units.zh: 今而位將軍，不可。」
units.en: To make him a general now is unacceptable."
units.literal: Now to make him a general—this cannot be."

units.zh: 帝不聽。
units.en: The emperor refused to listen.
units.literal: The emperor would not listen.

units.zh: 至僖宗立，始貶死。
units.en: Only when Xizong succeeded was Keji demoted and executed.
units.literal: Only when Emperor Xizong took the throne was Keji at last demoted and put to death.

units.zh: 方幸時，惟確屢言之。
units.en: While Keji was in favor, only Que spoke against him repeatedly.
units.literal: While favor lasted, only Que spoke of it repeatedly.

units.zh: 而神策中尉西門季玄者，亦剛鯁，謂可及曰：「汝以巧佞惑天子，當族滅！」
units.en: The Shence vice-director Ximen Jixuan was equally blunt; he told Keji, "You bewitch the emperor with flattery—your clan deserves extinction!"
units.literal: The Shence Army vice-director Ximen Jixuan was also stern and upright; he said to Keji: "You beguile the Son of Heaven with clever flattery—you deserve extermination of your clan!"

units.zh: 嘗見其受賜，謂曰：「今載以官車，後籍沒亦當爾。」
units.en: Seeing imperial gifts borne on official carts, he said, "Today they come by carriage; when your property is confiscated it will be the same."
units.literal: Once seeing him receive gifts, he said: "Today they are carried on official carts; later, when your property is confiscated, it will be the same."

units.zh: 確居位六年，進尚書右仆射，以同平章事出為鎮海節度使，徙河中，卒。
units.en: After six years Que was made right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, left office as chief minister to command Zhenhai, transferred to Hezhong, and died.
units.literal: After six years in office Que was advanced to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, left as chief minister to become military commissioner of Zhenhai, was transferred to Hezhong, and died.

units.zh: 始，畢諴與確同宰相，俱有雅望，世謂「曹畢」雲。
units.en: Bi Tan and Que had served together as chief ministers, both with fine reputations; people spoke of 'Cao and Bi.'
units.literal: At the beginning Bi Tan and Que served as chief ministers together; both had elegant reputations, and people called them 'Cao and Bi.'

units.zh: 弟汾，以忠武軍節度使入為戶部侍郎，判度支，卒。
units.en: His brother Fen came from Zhongwu as military commissioner to serve as vice minister of revenue overseeing the treasury, and died in office.
units.literal: His younger brother Fen entered the capital from military commissioner of Zhongwu as Vice Minister of Revenue with charge of the treasury and died in office.

units.zh: 劉瞻，字幾之，其先出彭城，後徙桂陽。
units.en: Liu Zhan, courtesy name Jizhi, came from Pengcheng and later moved to Guiyang.
units.literal: Liu Zhan, styled Jizhi, was originally from Pengcheng and later moved to Guiyang.

units.zh: 舉進士、博學宏詞，皆中。
units.en: He passed both the jinshi and the erudite literatus examinations.
units.literal: He passed the jinshi and the erudite literatus examinations, succeeding in both.

units.zh: 徐商辟署鹽鐵府，累遷太常博士。
units.en: Xu Shang recruited him to the Salt and Iron Commission; he rose to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: Xu Shang recruited him to the Salt and Iron Commission; he was promoted in succession to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 劉彖執政，薦為翰林學士，拜中書舍人，進承旨。
units.en: When Liu Cong was in power he recommended Zhan as Hanlin academician; Zhan became secretariat drafter and then chief drafting secretary.
units.literal: When Liu Cong held power he recommended Zhan as Hanlin academician; Zhan was appointed Secretariat Drafter and advanced to Chief Drafting Secretary.

units.zh: 出為河東節度使。
units.en: He was sent out as military commissioner of Hedong.
units.literal: He went out as military commissioner of Hedong.

units.zh: 咸通十一年，以中書侍郎同中書門下平章事。
units.en: In 870 he became vice director of the Secretariat and chief minister.
units.literal: In the eleventh year of Xiantong he became Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Director of the Chancellery.

units.zh: 同昌公主薨，懿宗捕太醫韓紹宗等送詔獄，逮系宗族數百人。
units.en: When Princess Tongchang died, Yizong arrested the court physicians Han Shaozong and others and imprisoned hundreds of their kinsmen.
units.literal: When Princess Tongchang died, Yizong arrested the imperial physicians Han Shaozong and others and sent them to the edict prison, seizing several hundred of their clansmen as well.

units.zh: 瞻喻諫官，皆依違無敢言，即自上疏固爭：「紹宗窮其術不能效，情有可矜。
units.en: Zhan urged the remonstrance officials, but none dared speak; he memorialized firmly: "Shaozong used every skill without success—he deserves pity.
units.literal: Zhan urged the remonstrance officials, but all were evasive and dared not speak; he himself submitted a memorial arguing firmly: "Shaozong exhausted his arts without effect—there is cause for compassion.

units.zh: 陛下徇愛女，囚平民，忿不顧難，取肆暴不明之謗。」
units.en: Your Majesty indulges grief for your daughter, imprisons commoners in rage, and invites the reproach of arbitrary cruelty."
units.literal: Your Majesty indulges love for your daughter, imprisons common people, and in anger disregards difficulty—you invite the reproach of wanton violence and lack of clarity."

units.zh: 帝大怒，即日賜罷，以檢校刑部尚書、同平章事為荊南節度使。
units.en: The emperor was furious and dismissed him the same day, sending him to Jingnan as honorary minister of justice with chief ministerial rank.
units.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and the same day granted his dismissal, making him honorary Minister of Justice with chief ministerial rank and military commissioner of Jingnan.

units.zh: 路巖、韋保衡從為惡言聞帝，俄斥廉州刺史。
units.en: Lu Yan and Wei Baoheng slandered him to the emperor, and he was soon demoted to prefect of Lianzhou.
units.literal: Lu Yan and Wei Baoheng followed with malicious words reaching the emperor, and soon Zhan was demoted to prefect of Lianzhou.

units.zh: 於是，翰林學士鄭畋以責詔不深切，御史中丞孫皇、諫議大夫高湘等坐與瞻善，分貶嶺南。
units.en: Hanlin academician Zheng Tian was punished for drafting too mild an edict; Vice Censor-in-Chief Sun Huang, Remonstrance Grandee Gao Xiang, and others were banished to Lingnan for their friendship with Zhan.
units.literal: Thereupon Hanlin academician Zheng Tian was punished because the reproving edict was not severe enough; Vice Censor-in-Chief Sun Huang, Remonstrance Grandee Gao Xiang, and others were implicated for friendship with Zhan and demoted separately to Lingnan.

units.zh: 巖等殊未慊，按圖視州道萬里，即貶州司戶參軍事，命李庾作詔極詆，將遂殺之。
units.en: Lu Yan and his allies were still unsatisfied; finding the prefecture ten thousand li away on the map, they demoted Zhan to army adjutant and had Li Yu draft a vicious edict, planning to kill him next.
units.literal: Lu Yan and the others were still not satisfied; consulting maps they saw the prefecture was ten thousand li distant and at once demoted Zhan to army adjutant of the prefecture; they ordered Li Yu to draft an edict of extreme vilification, intending next to kill him.

units.zh: 天下謂瞻鯁正，特為讒擠，舉以為冤。
units.en: The empire considered Zhan upright and wronged by slander alone.
units.literal: All under heaven said Zhan was upright and had been specially squeezed out by slander; everyone regarded it as a wrongful case.

units.zh: 幽州節度使張公素上疏申解，巖等不敢害。
units.en: Zhang Gongsu, military commissioner of Youzhou, memorialized in his defense; Lu Yan and his allies did not dare kill him.
units.literal: Zhang Gongsu, military commissioner of Youzhou, submitted a memorial pleading on his behalf; Lu Yan and the others did not dare harm him.

units.zh: 僖宗立，徙康、虢二州刺史，以刑部尚書召，復以中書侍郎平章事，居位三月卒。
units.en: When Xizong succeeded, Zhan was made prefect of Kang and Guo, recalled as minister of justice, restored as vice chancellor, served three months, and died.
units.literal: When Xizong took the throne, Zhan was moved to prefect of Kang and Guo; summoned as Minister of Justice, he again became Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chief Minister, held office three months, and died.

units.zh: 瞻為人廉約，所得俸以余濟親舊之窶困者，家不留儲。
units.en: Zhan lived frugally, gave his surplus salary to needy kin and friends, and kept no savings.
units.literal: Zhan was frugal and abstemious in person; he used the surplus of his salary to aid needy kin and friends and kept no stores at home.

units.zh: 無第舍，四方獻饋不及門，行己終始完潔。
units.en: He owned no mansion; gifts never reached his door; his conduct remained spotless to the end.
units.literal: He had no mansion; gifts from the four quarters did not reach his door; his conduct from beginning to end was whole and pure.

units.zh: 弟助，字元德，性仁孝，幼時與諸兄遊，至食飲，取最下者。
units.en: His younger brother Zhu, courtesy name Yuande, was kind and filial; as a boy playing with his brothers, he always took the smallest share at meals.
units.literal: His younger brother Zhu, styled Yuande, was benevolent and filial by nature; as a child playing with his elder brothers, when food and drink came he took the lowest portion.

units.zh: 及長，能文辭，喜黃老言。
units.en: Grown, he wrote well and favored Daoist teachings.
units.literal: When grown he could write well and delighted in Yellow Emperor and Laozi teachings.

units.zh: 年二十卒。
units.en: He died at twenty.
units.literal: He died at twenty.

units.zh: 李蔚，字茂休，系本隴西。
units.en: Li Wei, courtesy name Maoxiu, was of Longxi descent.
units.literal: Li Wei, styled Maoxiu, traced his lineage to Longxi.

units.zh: 舉進士、書判拔萃，皆中。
units.en: He passed both the jinshi and the distinguished document examination.
units.literal: He passed the jinshi and the distinguished document-examination, succeeding in both.

units.zh: 拜監察御史，擢累尚書右丞。
units.en: He became investigating censor and rose to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: He was appointed Investigating Censor and was promoted in succession to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 懿宗惑浮屠，常飯萬僧禁中，自為贊唄。
units.en: Yizong was obsessed with Buddhism, often feeding ten thousand monks in the palace and composing hymns himself.
units.literal: Yizong was deluded by Buddhism, often feeding ten thousand monks in the palace and himself composing hymns of praise.

units.zh: 蔚上疏切諫，引狄仁傑、姚元崇、辛替否所言，譏病時弊。
units.en: Wei memorialized sharply, citing Di Renjie, Yao Chong, and Xin Tifen and attacking the abuses of the day.
units.literal: Wei submitted a sharp memorial of remonstrance, citing what Di Renjie, Yao Chong, and Xin Tifen had said, and satirizing the ills of the age.

units.zh: 帝不聽，但以虛禮褒答。
units.en: The emperor ignored him and replied with empty praise.
units.literal: The emperor would not listen but answered only with empty courtesy and praise.

units.zh: 俄拜京兆尹、太常卿。
units.en: Soon he was made metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and minister of imperial sacrifices.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 出為宣武節度使，徙淮南。
units.en: He was posted to Xuanwu as military commissioner, then transferred to Huainan.
units.literal: He went out as military commissioner of Xuanwu and was transferred to Huainan.

units.zh: 代還，民詣闕請留，詔許一歲。
units.en: When his successor arrived, the people petitioned the throne to keep him; the court granted one more year.
units.literal: When his replacement returned, the people went to court to ask that he remain; an edict allowed one more year.

units.zh: 僖宗乾符初，以吏部尚書同中書門下平章事。
units.en: Early in Xizong's Qianfu reign he became minister of personnel and chief minister.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qianfu under Emperor Xizong he became Minister of Personnel and Co-Director of the Chancellery.

units.zh: 罷為東都留守。
units.en: He was made defender of the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: He was removed to serve as defender of the Eastern Capital.

units.zh: 河東亂，殺其帥崔季康，用邠寧李侃代之，士不附，以蔚嘗在太原府有惠政，為人所懷，拜河東節度使，同平章事。
units.en: Hedong mutinied and killed its commander Cui Jikang; Li Kan of Binning replaced him but the troops would not follow. Because Wei had once governed well in Taiyuan and was still beloved, he was made military commissioner of Hedong with chief ministerial rank.
units.literal: Hedong rebelled and killed its commander Cui Jikang; Li Kan of Binning was used to replace him, but the troops would not attach themselves. Because Wei had once served in the Taiyuan headquarters with benevolent administration and was remembered by the people, he was appointed military commissioner of Hedong with chief ministerial rank.

units.zh: 至鎮三日，卒。
units.en: He died three days after reaching his post.
units.literal: Three days after reaching his post he died.

units.zh: 始，懿宗成安國祠，賜寶坐二，度高二丈，構以沈檀，塗髹，鏤龍鳳葩蘤，金扣之，上施復坐，陳經幾其前，四隅立瑞鳥神人，高數尺，磴道以升，前被繡囊錦襜，珍麗精絕。
units.en: At first, Emperor Yizong completed the Anguo shrine and bestowed two jeweled seats, each two zhang high. They were made of agarwood and sandalwood, lacquered, carved with dragons, phoenixes, and flowers, and fitted with gold. Additional seats were placed above them and scripture tables before them; auspicious birds and divine figures several feet high stood at the four corners. Steps led up, while embroidered coverings and brocade valances draped the front. Their rarity and workmanship were unsurpassed.
units.literal: At first, Yizong completed the Anguo shrine and bestowed two jeweled seats measuring two zhang high. They were constructed of agarwood and sandalwood, coated with lacquer, carved with dragons, phoenixes, and flowers, and fastened with gold. Additional seats were set above them and scripture tables arranged before them. At the four corners stood auspicious birds and divine figures several feet high; steps provided access, and the front was covered with embroidered cloth and brocade valances. They were exceptionally rare, beautiful, and finely made.

units.zh: 咸通十四年春，詔迎佛骨鳳翔，或言：「昔憲宗嘗為此，俄晏駕。」
units.en: In the spring of 873 an edict ordered the Buddha's relic brought from Fengxiang; some warned, "Xianzong did the same and soon died."
units.literal: In the spring of the fourteenth year of Xiantong an edict ordered the Buddha's bone relic welcomed from Fengxiang; some said: "Formerly Xianzong once did this, and soon he died."

units.zh: 帝曰：「使朕生見之，死無恨！」
units.en: The emperor said, "Let me see it while I live, and I shall die without regret!"
units.literal: The emperor said: "Let me see it in life and I shall die without regret!"

units.zh: 乃以金銀為剎，珠玉為帳，孔鷸周飾之，小者尋丈，高至倍，刻檀為檐註，陛墄塗黃金，每一剎，數百人舉之。
units.en: Towers of gold and silver were built, canopies of pearl and jade, peacocks set round them; the smallest stood a full zhang, the tallest twice as high, with sandalwood eaves and gold-leafed terraces—each tower required hundreds of men to carry.
units.literal: Thereupon reliquary towers were made of gold and silver, canopies of pearls and jade, peacocks set all around as ornament; the small were a full zhang, the tall twice that; sandalwood was carved for eaves and pillars, steps and terraces coated with gold; for each tower several hundred men were needed to lift it.

units.zh: 香輿前後系道，綴珠瑟瑟幡蓋，殘彩以為幢節，費無貲限。
units.en: Incense chariots lined the road for miles, hung with pearl and kingfisher banners and pennants of leftover brocade—the cost was limitless.
units.literal: Incense chariots lined the road before and behind; pearl and kingfisher-feather banners and canopies were strung, leftover silks made into pennants and insignia—the expense knew no limit.

units.zh: 夏四月，至長安，彩觀夾路，其徒導衛。
units.en: In the fourth month it reached Chang'an; painted pavilions lined the road as the monks led the procession.
units.literal: In the fourth month of summer it reached Chang'an; painted pavilions lined the road, and the monks led the escort.

units.zh: 天子禦安福樓迎拜，至泣下。
units.en: The emperor went to the Anfu Tower to receive it and wept as he bowed.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven went to the Anfu Tower to welcome and bow, weeping as he did so.

units.zh: 詔賜兩街僧金幣，京師耆老及見元和事者，悉厚賜之。
units.en: Monks of both precincts received gold and coin by edict; elders of the capital who remembered the Yuanhe years were richly rewarded.
units.literal: An edict bestowed gold and coin on the monks of both monastic precincts; elders of the capital and all who had witnessed the Yuanhe era were richly rewarded.

units.zh: 不逞小人至斷臂指，流血滿道。
units.en: Desperate men even cut off their own arms and fingers until blood filled the streets.
units.literal: Lawless petty men even cut off arms and fingers until blood filled the road.

units.zh: 所過鄉聚，皆裒土為剎，相望於塗，爭以金翠抆飾。
units.en: Every village along the route built earthen reliquary towers, competing to adorn them with gold and jade.
units.literal: Every village and hamlet along the route heaped earth into reliquary towers, facing one another along the road, competing to adorn them with gold and kingfisher green.

units.zh: 傳言剎悉震搖，若有光景雲。
units.en: People said the towers trembled and glowed like clouds of light.
units.literal: Rumor said the towers all trembled and shook, as if with luminous clouds.

units.zh: 京師高貲相與集大衢，作繒臺縵闕，註水銀為池，金玉為樹木，聚桑門羅像，考鼓鳴螺繼日夜。
units.en: The rich of the capital gathered in the main avenues, building silk pavilions and brocade towers, pools of mercury and trees of gold and jade, with monks and Buddha images; drums and conches sounded day and night.
units.literal: The wealthy of the capital gathered in the great avenues, building silk platforms and brocade towers, pouring mercury for pools and gold and jade for trees, assembling monks and Buddha images, beating drums and sounding conches day and night without cease.

units.zh: 錦車繡輿，載歌舞從之。
units.en: Brocade carriages and embroidered litters carried singers and dancers in the train.
units.literal: Brocade carriages and embroidered palanquins carried singers and dancers in attendance.

units.zh: 秋七月，帝崩。
units.en: In the seventh month the emperor died.
units.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the emperor died.

units.zh: 方人主甘心篤向，如蔚言者甚多，皆不能救。
units.en: While the ruler devoted himself to the cult, many had remonstrated as Wei did, yet none could save him.
units.literal: Just as the ruler was willingly and devoutly inclined, many like Wei had spoken out, yet none could save him.

units.zh: 僖宗立，詔歸其骨，都人耆耋辭餞，或嗚咽流涕。
units.en: When Xizong succeeded, an edict sent the relic back; the elderly of the capital came to bid it farewell, many weeping.
units.literal: When Xizong took the throne, an edict ordered the relic returned; the aged of the capital came to bid farewell, some sobbing with tears.

units.zh: 贊曰：人之惑怪神也，甚哉！
units.en: The commentator says: How deeply people are deluded by the supernatural!
units.literal: The commentator says: How greatly people are deluded by strange spirits!

units.zh: 若佛者，特西域一槁人耳。
units.en: The Buddha was nothing but a gaunt man from the Western Regions.
units.literal: As for the Buddha, he was merely a withered man of the Western Regions.

units.zh: 裸顛露足，以乞食自資，臒辱其身，屏營山樊，行一概之苦，本無求於人，徒屬稍稍從之。
units.en: Bareheaded and barefoot, he lived by begging, emaciated and abased, dwelling in mountain seclusion and practicing austerity—he sought nothing from others, yet followers gradually gathered.
units.literal: Bareheaded, barefoot, he supported himself by begging, emaciated and abasing his body, dwelling apart in mountain fastnesses, practicing a single austerity—originally he sought nothing from others, yet followers little by little joined him.

units.zh: 然其言荒茫漫靡，夷幻變現，善推不驗無實之事，以鬼神死生貫為一條，據之不疑。
units.en: Yet his teachings were vast and vague, exotic and illusory; he excelled at speculating on unproved fantasies, weaving ghosts, death, and rebirth into one doctrine held without question.
units.literal: Yet his words were vast, vague, and diffuse, exotic and illusory in transformation; he was skilled at inferring unverified and unreal matters, threading ghosts and spirits with death and life into one strand, and holding to it without doubt.

units.zh: 掊嗜欲，棄親屬，大抵與黃老相出入。
units.en: He renounced desire and kin—much of his teaching overlapped with Daoism.
units.literal: He rejected desires and abandoned kin—on the whole his teaching overlapped with the Yellow Emperor and Laozi.

units.zh: 至漢十四葉，書入中國。
units.en: By the fourteenth Han emperor his texts had entered China.
units.literal: By the fourteenth generation of Han, his texts entered China.

units.zh: 跡夫生人之情，以耳目不際為奇，以不可知為神，以物理之外為畏，以變化無方為聖，以生而死、死復生、回復償報、歆艷其間為或然，以賤近貴遠為。
units.en: Human nature prizes what lies beyond sight and hearing, calls the unknowable divine, fears what lies outside natural law, reveres boundless change, accepts death and rebirth with karmic reward as possible, and scorns the near while honoring the distant.
units.literal: Tracing the feelings of living humanity: what lies beyond sight and hearing is deemed marvelous; what cannot be known is deemed divine; what lies outside physical law is deemed fearful; what changes without limit is deemed holy; that life leads to death, death to life again, and retribution and reward cycle through it is deemed possible; to despise the near and honor the distant is deemed right.

units.zh: 鞮譯差殊，不可研詰。
units.en: Foreign transliterations differ so widely they cannot be rigorously examined.
units.literal: Transliteration from foreign tongues differs and cannot be closely examined.

units.zh: 華人之譎誕者，又攘莊周、列禦寇之說佐其高，層累架騰，直出其表，以無上不可加為勝，妄相誇脅而倡其風。
units.en: Crafty Chinese then borrowed Zhuangzi and Liezi to exalt it further, building tower upon tower until it soared beyond measure, vaunting the supreme and coercing one another to spread the cult.
units.literal: Crafty and extravagant Chinese then seized the doctrines of Zhuang Zhou and Lie Yukou to elevate it further, piling layer upon layer until it soared straight beyond the norm, taking 'nothing higher can be added' as victory, wildly boasting and coercing one another to spread the fashion.

units.zh: 於是，自天子逮庶人，皆震動而祠奉之。
units.en: Thereupon emperor and commoner alike were moved to worship it.
units.literal: Thereupon, from the Son of Heaven down to commoners, all were stirred to worship and serve it.

units.zh: 初，宰相王縉以緣業事佐代宗，於是始作內道場，晝夜梵唄，冀禳寇戎，大作盂蘭，肖祖宗像，分供塔廟，為賊臣嘻笑。
units.en: At first, Chief Minister Wang Jin supported Emperor Daizong with teachings about karma and merit. The palace then established an inner ritual sanctuary where Buddhist chants sounded day and night in hopes of warding off enemy armies. Grand Ullambana rites were held, images of the imperial ancestors were made and distributed among pagodas and temples, and rebel officials laughed at the spectacle.
units.literal: At first Chief Minister Wang Jin, with karma and merit, assisted Emperor Daizong; then the inner dharma hall was first established, day and night chanting sutras, hoping to avert invaders; the Ullambana festival was greatly performed, images of ancestors fashioned and distributed to pagodas and temples—making rebel ministers laugh.

units.zh: 至憲宗世，遂迎佛骨於鳳翔，內之宮中。
units.en: Under Xianzong the Buddha's relic was brought from Fengxiang into the palace.
units.literal: By Xianzong's time the Buddha's bone relic was welcomed from Fengxiang and installed within the palace.

units.zh: 韓愈指言其弊，帝怒，竄愈瀕死，憲亦弗獲天年。
units.en: Han Yu exposed its harm; the emperor banished him nearly to death—and Xianzong too died before his time.
units.literal: Han Yu pointed out its harm; the emperor was enraged and banished Yu nearly to death—and Xianzong too did not attain his full span of years.

units.zh: 幸福而禍，無亦左乎！
units.en: Blessing turned to disaster—is this not perverse!
units.literal: Blessing turned to calamity—is this not perverse!

units.zh: 懿宗不君，精爽奪迷，復蹈前車而覆之。
units.en: Yizong was no true ruler; his mind was lost to delusion, and he repeated his predecessors' ruin.
units.literal: Yizong was no true ruler; his spirit was seized and deluded, and he again followed the overturned cart of his predecessors.

units.zh: 興哀無知之場，丐庇百解之胔，以死自誓，無有顧藉，流淚拜伏，雖事宗廟上帝，無以進焉。
units.en: He raised a lament before an insensible thing and begged protection from the disjointed remains of a corpse. Pledging himself to it unto death without thought of restraint, he wept and prostrated himself with a devotion that even worship of the ancestral temple and the Lord on High could not surpass.
units.literal: He raised a lament before an insensible thing and begged protection from the disjointed remains of a corpse. Pledging himself to it unto death without restraint, he wept and prostrated himself with a devotion that even service to the ancestral temple and the Lord on High could not surpass.

units.zh: 屈萬乘之貴，自等於古胡，數千載而遠，以身為徇。
units.en: He debased imperial dignity, equated himself with barbarians of ages past, and offered his body as sacrifice.
units.literal: He humbled the dignity of the myriad chariots, equated himself with ancient barbarians thousands of years distant, and offered his person as sacrifice.

units.zh: 嗚呼，運祚殫，天告之矣！
units.en: Alas, the dynasty's fortune was spent—Heaven had declared it!
units.literal: Alas, the dynasty's fortune was exhausted—Heaven had proclaimed it!

units.zh: 懿不三月而徂，唐德之不競，厥有來哉，悲夫！
units.en: Yizong died within three months; that Tang virtue had waned had long been foretold—how lamentable!
units.literal: Yi was gone in less than three months; that Tang virtue could not prevail had long been coming—how lamentable!
